newsitem.title: USA: Phila. sues state over school financing -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Phila. sues state over school financing -- paper.

text.p: Philadelphia and the city's school district sued Pennsylvania Monday in a class action lawsuit, demanding millions more in school funding, Philadelphia Inquirer reported Tuesday.

The suit, joined by local advocacy groups, alleges that Pennsylvania provides an inadequate education in public schools, and it asks the Commonwealth Court to force the state to pay $53 million more this year alone to help reform the system.
The district also said it is preparing a civil rights lawsuit attempting to get more money through the U.S. District Court.
Pennsylvania Association of Rural and Small Schools has filed a similar suit in Commonwealth Court attacking the state's method of financing public education.

Last year, the court ruled in a separate case that the state had to pay to help desegregate and reform schools, but that ruling is under appeal. The state contends its system is fair and maybe even more generous to Philadelphia than to other local districts.

In secondary trading Tuesday, Philadelphia School District AMBAC 5.50s of 2018 were offered at a 5.65 percent net. J.J. Kenny Evaluation Services priced the bonds at Monday's close at a 5.62 percent yield.
